title: Cohort and Segment Slicing Analysis
description: Decomposition of aggregate metrics into homogenous sub-populations to identify hidden disparities.
conditions: Dataset contains heterogeneous sub-populations (e.g., patient cohorts, geographic regions, tier plans)
Suspected Simpson's Paradox where aggregate trend inverts within subgroups
Business requirement for personalized or targeted insights
recommended_methods: Multi-dimensional groupby slicing across primary demographic/operational dimensions
Variance across segment metrics vs overall population mean
Simpson's Paradox detection across stratified contingency tables
selection_rules: Prioritize segment dimensions that maximize inter-segment metric variance
Ensure minimum segment sample size (N >= 30) before reporting segment-specific conclusions
If aggregate trend contradicts subgroup trends, highlight Simpson's Paradox prominently
limitations: Over-segmentation leads to data fragmentation, loss of statistical power, and false discoveries
Arbitrary segment cutoffs on continuous features can hide non-linear boundary effects
